segments.arabic: [615] حدثنا أبو نعيم قال: حدثنا شيبان عن يحيى قال: سمعت أبا سلمة يقول أخبرنا جابر بن عبد الله
segments.english: Abu Nu‘aym related to us. He said: Shayban related to us, from Yahya, who said: I heard Abu Salamah say: Jabir ibn ‘Abd Allah informed us:

segments.arabic: أن النبي ﷺ جاءه عمر بن الخطاب يوم الخندق، فقال: يا رسول الله والله ما كدت أن أصلي حتى كادت الشمس تغرب وذلك بعد ما أفطر الصائم، فقال النبي ﷺ والله ما صليتها فنزل النبي ﷺ إلى بطحان وأنا معه فتوضأ ثم صلى يعني العصر بعد ما غربت الشمس ثم صلى بعدها المغرب
segments.english: That ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab came to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, on the Day of the Trench and said: “Messenger of Allah, by Allah, I had scarcely managed to pray before the sun was about to set.” That was after the fasting person had broken his fast. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “By Allah, I have not prayed it.” The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, went down to Buthan, and I was with him. He performed ablution and then prayed—meaning ‘Asr—after the sun had set, then prayed Maghrib after it.

notes: The selected Arabic retains both scarcely/about-to constructions, the statement that this occurred after the fasting person broke his fast, all three honorifics, the Prophet’s oath and the narrator’s meaning ‘Asr. Bewley adds cursing Quraysh not present here; the pinned Khan-family comparison omits the Prophet’s oath. Neither difference is silently imported. The historical print directly names ‘Asr in the final clause while the digital and modern print retain the narrator’s means ‘Asr aside.

segments.arabic: [616] حدثنا أبو معمر عبد الله بن عمرو قال: حدثنا عبد الوارث قال: حدثنا عبد العزيز بن صهيب عن أنس قال
segments.english: Abu Ma‘mar ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Amr related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Warith related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-‘Aziz ibn Suhayb related to us, from Anas, who said:

segments.arabic: أقيمت الصلاة والنبي ﷺ يناجي رجلا في جانب المسجد فما قام إلى الصلاة حتى نام القوم
segments.english: The iqamah was given while the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was speaking privately to a man at the side of the mosque. He did not stand for prayer until the people had fallen asleep.

notes: The full Abu Ma‘mar ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Amr name, private conversation, side of the mosque and until the people slept remain. The comparison’s some and sitting-posture explanation are not added. The historical print inserts هو before Ibn Suhayb; selected digital and modern wording remain.

segments.arabic: [617] حدثنا عياش بن الوليد قال: حدثنا عبد الأعلى قال: حدثنا حميد
segments.english: ‘Ayyash ibn al-Walid related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-A‘la related to us. He said: Humayd related to us.

segments.arabic: قال: سألت ثابتا البناني عن الرجل يتكلم بعد ما تقام الصلاة فحدثني عن أنس بن مالك قال
segments.english: He said: I asked Thabit al-Bunani about a man speaking after the iqamah had been given. He related to me, from Anas ibn Malik, who said:

segments.arabic: أقيمت الصلاة فعرض للنبي ﷺ رجل فحبسه بعد ما أقيمت الصلاة
segments.english: The iqamah was given, and a man approached the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and detained him after the iqamah had been given.

notes: Humayd’s full question to Thabit al-Bunani and the ensuing Anas report remain, as does the repeated after-the-iqamah clause. The modern print additionally repeats al-Hasan’s statement adjacent to this entry; the selected digital source and historical print place it under the following chapter. That chapter material remains separate and is not folded into the narration.

segments.arabic: [618] حدثنا عبد الله بن يوسف قال: أخبرنا مالك عن أبي الزناد عن الأعرج عن أبي هريرة أن رسول الله ﷺ قال:
segments.english: ‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A‘raj, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

segments.arabic: والذي نفسي بيده لقد هممت أن آمر بحطب فيحطب ثم آمر بالصلاة فيؤذن لها ثم آمر رجلا فيؤم الناس ثم أخالف إلى رجال فأحرق عليهم بيوتهم والذي نفسي بيده لو يعلم أحدهم أنه يجد عرقا سمينا أو مرماتين حسنتين لشهد العشاء
segments.english: “By Him in whose hand is my soul, I considered ordering firewood to be gathered, then ordering the prayer and having its adhan called, then ordering a man to lead the people, then going to some men and burning their houses down upon them. By Him in whose hand is my soul, if one of them knew that he would find a meaty bone or two good pieces of meat from between a sheep’s hooves, he would attend ‘Isha’.”

notes: Both oaths and the complete sequence of contemplated actions remain; no action is changed from contemplated to performed. The source does not append an explanatory non-attendance clause to some men. The two English comparisons differ on مرماتين: Bewley gives hooves, while the pinned Khan-family text gives meat between ribs. Ibn Hajar records meat between sheep’s hooves and an alternative arrows interpretation. The working rendering selects the former lexical sense with an explicit uncertainty notice. No ruling or reader instruction is supplied by the app.

segments.arabic: [619] حدثنا عبد الله بن يوسف قال: أخبرنا مالك عن نافع عن عبد الله بن عمر أن رسول الله ﷺ قال:
segments.english: ‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Nafi‘, from ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Umar, that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

segments.arabic: صلاة الجماعة تفضل صلاة الفذ بسبع وعشرين درجة
segments.english: “Congregational prayer surpasses the prayer of a person alone by twenty-seven degrees.”

notes: This is the first of two separate digital paragraphs labelled 619. Its reader reference remains 619; the following Abu Sa‘id report is explicitly mapped to 619b, without shifting later references. The full Ibn ‘Umar chain and twenty-seven degrees remain. The historical print spans pages 168–169; the modern print calls this 645. The Khan-family comparison is 1.11.618, individually matched rather than inferred from a global numbering offset.

segments.arabic: [619] حدثنا عبد الله بن يوسف قال: أخبرنا الليث حدثني ابن الهاد عن عبد الله بن خباب عن أبي سعيد الخدري أنه سمع النبي ﷺ يقول:
segments.english: ‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Al-Layth informed us: Ibn al-Had related to me, from ‘Abd Allah ibn Khabbab, from Abu Sa‘id al-Khudri, that he heard the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, say:

segments.arabic: صلاة الجماعة تفضل صلاة الفذ بخمس وعشرين درجة
segments.english: “Congregational prayer surpasses the prayer of a person alone by twenty-five degrees.”

notes: This is the second original 619 paragraph, a distinct Abu Sa‘id al-Khudri report with twenty-five degrees. The explicit source map assigns reader reference 619b and retains the original [619] label and paragraph identity. Bewley also labels this 619b; the Khan-family comparison is 1.11.619 and the modern print is 646. The historical print expands Ibn al-Had to Yazid ibn al-Had and uses related to us for al-Layth; the digital and modern reading informed us, Ibn al-Had related to me remains. The two reports are never combined or silently renumbered.

segments.arabic: [620] حدثنا موسى بن إسماعيل قال: حدثنا عبد الواحد قال: حدثنا الأعمش قال: سمعت أبا صالح يقول: سمعت أبا هريرة يقول: قال رسول الله ﷺ:
segments.english: Musa ibn Isma‘il related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Wahid related to us. He said: Al-A‘mash related to us. He said: I heard Abu Salih say: I heard Abu Hurayrah say: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

segments.arabic: صلاة الرجل في الجماعة تضعف على صلاته في بيته وفي سوقه خمسة وعشرين ضعفا وذلك أنه إذا توضأ فأحسن الوضوء ثم خرج إلى المسجد لا يخرجه إلا الصلاة لم يخط خطوة إلا رفعت له بها درجة وحط عنه بها خطيئة فإذا صلى لم تزل الملائكة تصلي عليه ما دام في مصلاه اللهم صل عليه اللهم ارحمه ولا يزال أحدكم في صلاة ما انتظر الصلاة
segments.english: “A man’s prayer in congregation is multiplied twenty-five times over his prayer in his house and in his marketplace. That is because, when he performs ablution and performs it well, then goes out to the mosque with nothing taking him out except prayer, he takes no step without being raised a degree by it and having a sin removed from him by it. When he prays, the angels continue to pray for him as long as he is in his place of prayer: ‘O Allah, bless him. O Allah, have mercy on him.’ And one of you continues to be in prayer as long as he waits for prayer.”

notes: The prayer in his house and his marketplace, good ablution, sole purpose of going out, each step raising a degree and removing a sin, and waiting for prayer remain. The selected Arabic and both prints say bless him in the angels’ first supplication; Bewley says forgive him. Bless him is retained, distinct from forgive him at 628. The explanatory additions accounts of deeds and alone in the Khan-family comparison are not inserted.

segments.arabic: [621] حدثنا أبو اليمان قال: أخبرنا شعيب عن الزهري قال: أخبرني سعيد بن المسيب وأبو سلمة بن عبد الرحمن أن أبا هريرة قال: سمعت رسول الله ﷺ يقول:
segments.english: Abu al-Yaman related to us. He said: Shu‘ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: Sa‘id ibn al-Musayyab and Abu Salamah ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman informed me that Abu Hurayrah said: I heard the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, say:

segments.arabic: تفضل صلاة الجميع صلاة أحدكم وحده بخمسة وعشرين جزءا وتجتمع ملائكة الليل وملائكة النهار في صلاة الفجر
segments.english: “Congregational prayer surpasses the prayer of one of you alone by twenty-five parts. The angels of the night and the angels of the day gather at the Fajr prayer.”

segments.arabic: ثم يقول أبو هريرة فاقرؤوا إن شئتم { إن قرآن الفجر كان مشهودا }
segments.english: Then Abu Hurayrah says: “Recite, if you wish: ‘Indeed, the recitation at dawn is witnessed.’”

segments.arabic: قال شعيب وحدثني نافع عن عبد الله بن عمر قال تفضلها بسبع وعشرين درجة
segments.english: Shu‘ayb said: And Nafi‘ related to me, from ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Umar, who said: “It surpasses it by twenty-seven degrees.”

notes: The full chain retains both Sa‘id ibn al-Musayyab and Abu Salamah ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman. The twenty-five parts, meeting of the two groups of angels, Abu Hurayrah’s attributed recitation and Shu‘ayb’s complete Nafi‘/Ibn ‘Umar route with twenty-seven degrees remain separately ordered. The modern print gives the closing route its own number 649; the selected digital and historical grouping remain one entry. The pinned Khan-family text prints the verse reference as 17.18; no comparison reference or added recitation label is inserted into the selected wording.

segments.arabic: [622] حدثنا عمر بن حفص قال: حدثنا أبي قال: حدثنا الأعمش قال: سمعت سالما قال: سمعت أم الدرداء تقول
segments.english: ‘Umar ibn Hafs related to us. He said: My father related to us. He said: Al-A‘mash related to us. He said: I heard Salim say: I heard Umm al-Darda’ say:

segments.arabic: دخل علي أبو الدرداء وهو مغضب فقلت: ما أغضبك، فقال والله ما أعرف من أمة محمد ﷺ شيئا إلا أنهم يصلون جميعا
segments.english: Abu al-Darda’ came in to me while he was angry. I said: “What has angered you?” He said: “By Allah, I recognize nothing of the community of Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, except that they pray together.”

notes: The angry arrival, question, oath, community of Muhammad and source honorific remain. The report is attributed to Umm al-Darda’ about Abu al-Darda’; it is not presented as a new saying of the Prophet. The historical circumstances and good-things explanation appended by the Khan-family comparison are not part of the selected Arabic and are not added.

segments.arabic: [623] حدثنا محمد بن العلاء قال: حدثنا أبو أسامة عن بريد بن عبد الله عن أبي بردة عن أبي موسى قال: قال النبي ﷺ
segments.english: Muhammad ibn al-‘Ala’ related to us. He said: Abu Usamah related to us, from Burayd ibn ‘Abd Allah, from Abu Burdah, from Abu Musa, who said: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

segments.arabic: أعظم الناس أجرا في الصلاة أبعدهم فأبعدهم ممشى والذي ينتظر الصلاة حتى يصليها مع الإمام أعظم أجرا من الذي يصلي ثم ينام
segments.english: “Those with the greatest reward for prayer are those who walk the farthest, then the next farthest. One who waits for prayer until he prays it with the imam has a greater reward than one who prays and then sleeps.”

notes: The complete chain retains Burayd ibn ‘Abd Allah and Abu Burdah. The repeated farthest/next farthest walking comparison and the contrast between waiting for the imam and praying then sleeping remain. The English comparison’s geographical parenthesis is not added. The historical print uses related to me for Abu Usamah; the selected digital and modern witness say related to us.

segments.arabic: [624] حدثنا قتيبة عن مالك عن سمي مولى أبي بكر عن أبي صالح السمان عن أبي هريرة أن رسول الله ﷺ قال:
segments.english: Qutaybah related to us, from Malik, from Sumayy, the freedman of Abu Bakr, from Abu Salih al-Samman, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

segments.arabic: بينما رجل يمشي بطريق وجد غصن شوك على الطريق فأخره فشكر الله له فغفر له، ثم قال الشهداء خمسة المطعون والمبطون والغريق وصاحب الهدم والشهيد في سبيل الله، وقال لو يعلم الناس ما في النداء والصف الأول ثم لم يجدوا إلا أن يستهموا لاستهموا عليه ولو يعلمون ما في التهجير لاستبقوا إليه ولو يعلمون ما في العتمة والصبح لأتوهما ولو حبوا
segments.english: “While a man was walking along a road, he found a thorny branch on the road and moved it aside. Allah appreciated his deed and forgave him.” Then he said: “The martyrs are five: one who dies of plague, one who dies of an abdominal illness, one who drowns, one who dies under a collapsed structure, and one martyred in the path of Allah.” And he said: “If people knew what there is in the call and the first row, then found no way except to draw lots, they would draw lots for it. If they knew what there is in going early, they would race to it. If they knew what there is in ‘Isha’ and the dawn prayer, they would come to them even crawling.”

notes: All three connected statements remain: the removed thorny branch, the five martyr categories, and the call/first row, early attendance, and night/dawn prayer clauses. The modern print labels portions 652–654; the selected digital and historical print retain this as one complete entry. The body says going early without explicitly naming Zuhr; the chapter names Zuhr and remains separate, unlike the comparison’s inserted prayer label. Sumayy’s patron is Abu Bakr in the selected digital and modern print; the historical print expands this to Abu Bakr ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman and adds an honorific after the path-of-Allah clause. Those additions are not silently imported.

segments.arabic: [625] حدثنا محمد بن عبد الله بن حوشب قال: حدثنا عبد الوهاب قال: حدثنا حميد عن أنس قال: قال النبي ﷺ
segments.english: Muhammad ibn ‘Abd Allah ibn Hawshab related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Wahhab related to us. He said: Humayd related to us, from Anas, who said: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

segments.arabic: يا بني سلمة ألا تحتسبون آثاركم،
segments.english: “Banu Salimah, will you not seek reward for your footsteps?”

segments.arabic: وقال مجاهد في قوله { ونكتب ما قدموا وآثارهم } قال خطاهم،
segments.english: And Mujahid said concerning His words, “And We record what they have sent ahead and their traces”: He said: “Their footsteps.”

segments.arabic: وقال ابن أبي مريم أخبرنا يحيى بن أيوب حدثني حميد حدثني أنس
segments.english: And Ibn Abi Maryam said: Yahya ibn Ayyub informed us. Humayd related to me. Anas related to me:

segments.arabic: أن بني سلمة أرادوا أن يتحولوا عن منازلهم فينزلوا قريبا من النبي ﷺ قال: فكره رسول الله ﷺ أن يعروا المدينة، فقال ألا تحتسبون آثاركم
segments.english: That Banu Salimah wanted to move from their homes and settle near the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. He said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, disliked their leaving Madinah deserted, and said: “Will you not seek reward for your footsteps?”

segments.arabic: قال مجاهد خطاهم آثارهم أن يمشي في الأرض بأرجلهم
segments.english: Mujahid said: “Their footsteps are their traces: walking on the earth with their feet.”

notes: Both inspected prints explicitly read أن يعروا المدينة, while the selected digital text omits المدينة. Only that missing place name is restored with before/after evidence and a visible notice, retaining the original input. Bewley describes moving to Madinah; the Khan-family comparison describes leaving their houses uninhabited. The working rendering follows the inspected Arabic wording: leaving Madinah deserted.

Both of Mujahid’s comments and Ibn Abi Maryam’s full additional chain remain separate and in source order. The digital source says Anas related to me in the second chain, while both prints have from Anas; this difference is recorded, not silently harmonized. The historical print also names Anas ibn Malik and the Messenger of Allah in the first route, and uses a different opening formula for Ibn Abi Maryam; the modern print numbers the latter route 656. The closing digital أن يمشي and the printed أن المشي / أو المشي variants are not silently rewritten. All three selected honorifics and both footsteps questions remain.

segments.arabic: [626] حدثنا عمر بن حفص قال: حدثنا أبي قال: حدثنا الأعمش قال: حدثني أبو صالح عن أبي هريرة قال: قال النبي ﷺ
segments.english: ‘Umar ibn Hafs related to us. He said: My father related to us. He said: Al-A‘mash related to us. He said: Abu Salih related to me, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

segments.arabic: ليس صلاة أثقل على المنافقين من الفجر والعشاء ولو يعلمون ما فيهما لأتوهما ولو حبوا لقد هممت أن آمر المؤذن فيقيم ثم آمر رجلا يؤم الناس ثم آخذ شعلا من نار فأحرق على من لا يخرج إلى الصلاة بعد
segments.english: “No prayer is heavier upon the hypocrites than Fajr and ‘Isha’. If they knew what there is in them, they would come to them even crawling. I considered ordering the caller to give the iqamah, then ordering a man to lead the people, then taking flames of fire and setting fire to those who have not yet gone out to prayer.”

notes: The complete Fajr/‘Isha’ comparison, even-crawling clause, contemplated iqamah/leader/fire sequence and final not-yet qualification remain. The text records contemplation, not an action performed. The selected source does not explicitly name houses here, unlike the prior 618 report and the explanatory Khan-family wording. No new ruling or instruction is supplied by the app.

segments.arabic: [627] حدثنا مسدد قال: حدثنا يزيد بن زريع قال: حدثنا خالد عن أبي قلابة عن مالك بن الحويرث عن النبي ﷺ قال:
segments.english: Musaddad related to us. He said: Yazid ibn Zuray‘ related to us. He said: Khalid related to us, from Abu Qilabah, from Malik ibn al-Huwayrith, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

segments.arabic: إذا حضرت الصلاة فأذنا وأقيما ثم ليؤمكما أكبركما
segments.english: “When the time for prayer comes, let the two of you give the adhan and the iqamah, then let the older of you lead you.”

notes: The dual commands for the two people and the older of them leading remain; no caller is invented or second person removed. The full Malik ibn al-Huwayrith chain remains despite the English comparisons’ abbreviated chains.

segments.arabic: [628] حدثنا عبد الله بن مسلمة عن مالك عن أبي الزناد عن الأعرج عن أبي هريرة أن رسول الله ﷺ قال:
segments.english: ‘Abd Allah ibn Maslamah related to us, from Malik, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A‘raj, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

segments.arabic: الملائكة تصلي على أحدكم ما دام في مصلاه ما لم يحدث اللهم اغفر له اللهم ارحمه لا يزال أحدكم في صلاة ما دامت الصلاة تحبسه لا يمنعه أن ينقلب إلى أهله إلا الصلاة
segments.english: “The angels pray for one of you as long as he is in his place of prayer and has not broken his ablution: ‘O Allah, forgive him. O Allah, have mercy on him.’ One of you continues to be in prayer as long as prayer detains him, with nothing preventing him from returning to his family except prayer.”

notes: The source’s condition of not breaking ablution and the two supplications remain. Unlike 620, the first supplication is explicitly forgive him. The final two clauses retain prayer detaining him and its being the only thing preventing his return to his family. The Khan-family example of passing wind remains comparison explanation and is not inserted.

segments.arabic: [629] حدثنا محمد بن بشار قال: حدثنا يحيى عن عبيد الله قال: حدثني خبيب بن عبد الرحمن عن حفص بن عاصم عن أبي هريرة عن النبي ﷺ قال:
segments.english: Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us. He said: Yahya related to us, from ‘Ubayd Allah, who said: Khubayb ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman related to me, from Hafs ibn ‘Asim, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

segments.arabic: سبعة يظلهم الله في ظله يوم لا ظل إلا ظله الإمام العادل وشاب نشأ في عبادة ربه ورجل قلبه معلق في المساجد ورجلان تحابا في الله اجتمعا عليه وتفرقا عليه ورجل طلبته امرأة ذات منصب وجمال، فقال إني أخاف الله ورجل تصدق أخفى حتى لا تعلم شماله ما تنفق يمينه ورجل ذكر الله خاليا ففاضت عيناه
segments.english: “Seven will Allah shade in His shade on a day when there is no shade except His shade: a just imam; a young person who grew up worshipping his Lord; a man whose heart is attached to the mosques; two men who loved one another for Allah’s sake, meeting on that basis and parting on that basis; a man whom a woman of rank and beauty sought, who said, ‘I fear Allah’; a man who gave charity and concealed it so that his left hand did not know what his right hand spent; and a man who remembered Allah alone, and his eyes overflowed.”

notes: All seven people and all identifying clauses remain in their source order. His shade is not expanded to a reference to the Throne. His Lord, mosques in the plural, the meeting/parting clauses, the woman’s rank and beauty, left/right hands and solitary remembrance remain. The specific illicit-intercourse wording and parenthetical interpretations in the Khan-family comparison are not added to the selected Arabic. The source names Khubayb ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman, with related to me.

segments.arabic: [630] حدثنا قتيبة قال: حدثنا إسماعيل بن جعفر عن حميد قال:
segments.english: Qutaybah related to us. He said: Isma‘il ibn Ja‘far related to us, from Humayd, who said:

segments.arabic: وسئل أنس هل اتخذ رسول الله ﷺ خاتما،
segments.english: And Anas was asked: “Did the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, have a ring?”

segments.arabic: فقال: نعم أخر ليلة صلاة العشاء إلى شطر الليل ثم أقبل علينا بوجهه بعد ما صلى، فقال صلى الناس ورقدوا ولم تزالوا في صلاة منذ انتظرتموها قال: فكأني أنظر إلى وبيص خاتمه
segments.english: He said: “Yes. One night he delayed the ‘Isha’ prayer until halfway through the night. Then, after he had prayed, he turned his face towards us and said: ‘The people have prayed and slept, and you have continued to be in prayer since you began waiting for it.’” He said: “It is as though I am looking at the gleam of his ring.”

notes: Humayd’s account of the question to Anas stays visible as a transmission note, followed by Anas’s answer; it is not hidden inside the chain or reattributed to the Prophet. The delay until half the night, turning towards the listeners after praying, the people having prayed and slept, and the final first-person gleam-of-the-ring recollection remain. The comparison’s on-that-day addition is absent from the selected Arabic.

segments.arabic: [631] حدثنا علي بن عبد الله قال: حدثنا يزيد بن هارون قال: أخبرنا محمد بن مطرف عن زيد بن أسلم عن عطاء بن يسار عن أبي هريرة عن النبي ﷺ قال:
segments.english: ‘Ali ibn ‘Abd Allah related to us. He said: Yazid ibn Harun related to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Mutarrif informed us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from ‘Ata’ ibn Yasar, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

segments.arabic: من غدا إلى المسجد وراح أعد الله له نزله من الجنة كلما غدا أو راح
segments.english: “Whoever goes to the mosque in the morning and in the evening, Allah prepares hospitality for him in Paradise each time he goes in the morning or the evening.”

notes: The selected digital and modern print use and in the first morning/evening clause, then or in the final each-time clause. The historical print uses or in both; the selected distinction remains. Bewley renders nuzul as residence and the Khan-family text combines place and hospitality. Ibn al-Mulaqqin explains the term as hospitality prepared for a guest, and records both time-of-day and broader going/returning senses. This working translation selects morning/evening and hospitality; no palace, size of reward or additional instruction is supplied.

segments.arabic: [632] حدثنا عبد العزيز بن عبد الله قال: حدثنا إبراهيم بن سعد عن أبيه عن حفص بن عاصم عن عبد الله بن مالك بن بحينة قال
segments.english: ‘Abd al-‘Aziz ibn ‘Abd Allah related to us. He said: Ibrahim ibn Sa‘d related to us, from his father, from Hafs ibn ‘Asim, from ‘Abd Allah ibn Malik ibn Buhaynah, who said:

segments.arabic: مر النبي ﷺ برجل
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, passed by a man.

segments.arabic: قال وحدثني عبد الرحمن قال: حدثنا بهز بن أسد قال: حدثنا شعبة قال: أخبرني سعد بن إبراهيم قال: سمعت حفص بن عاصم قال: سمعت رجلا من الأزد يقال له مالك بن بحينة
segments.english: He said: And ‘Abd al-Rahman related to me. He said: Bahz ibn Asad related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us. He said: Sa‘d ibn Ibrahim informed me. He said: I heard Hafs ibn ‘Asim say: I heard a man from al-Azd called Malik ibn Buhaynah say:

segments.arabic: أن رسول الله ﷺ رأى رجلا وقد أقيمت الصلاة يصلي ركعتين فلما انصرف رسول الله ﷺ لاث به الناس، وقال له رسول الله ﷺ الصبح أربعا الصبح أربعا
segments.english: That the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, saw a man praying two rak‘ahs when the iqamah had been given. When the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, had finished, the people gathered around him, and the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said to him: “The dawn prayer as four? The dawn prayer as four?”

segments.arabic: تابعه غندر ومعاذ عن شعبة في مالك، وقال ابن إسحاق عن سعد عن حفص عن عبد الله بن بحينة، وقال حماد أخبرنا سعد عن حفص عن مالك
segments.english: Ghundar and Mu‘adh corroborated it from Shu‘bah concerning Malik. And Ibn Ishaq said: From Sa‘d, from Hafs, from ‘Abd Allah ibn Buhaynah. And Hammad said: Sa‘d informed us, from Hafs, from Malik.

notes: Both full opening routes, the first route’s brief opening, the repeated dawn-prayer question and all three closing transmission notes remain. The selected source names ‘Abd Allah ibn Malik ibn Buhaynah in the first route, Malik ibn Buhaynah in the second, ‘Abd Allah ibn Buhaynah in Ibn Ishaq’s note and Malik in Hammad’s note. These forms are not harmonized. Ibn Hajar discusses the naming discrepancy and the maternal name; the English comparisons abbreviate the routes and closing notes.

The digital source and historical print say concerning Malik in the Ghundar/Mu‘adh note; the modern print has from Malik. The pronoun in people gathered around him remains unexpanded: Ibn Hajar explicitly records competing antecedents. The English does not settle the pronoun through an inserted name. Brill 171 contains the beginning of the chain, continued on 172.

segments.arabic: [633] حدثنا عمر بن حفص بن غياث قال: حدثني أبي قال: حدثنا الأعمش عن إبراهيم قال الأسود قال
segments.english: ‘Umar ibn Hafs ibn Ghiyath related to us. He said: My father related to me. He said: Al-A‘mash related to us, from Ibrahim, who said: Al-Aswad said:

segments.arabic: كنا عند عائشة رضى الله تعالى عنها فذكرنا المواظبة على الصلاة والتعظيم لها قالت لما مرض رسول الله ﷺ مرضه الذي مات فيه فحضرت الصلاة فأذن، فقال مروا أبا بكر فليصل بالناس فقيل له إن أبا بكر رجل أسيف إذا قام في مقامك لم يستطع أن يصلي بالناس وأعاد فأعادوا له فأعاد الثالثة، فقال إنكن صواحب يوسف مروا أبا بكر فليصل بالناس فخرج أبو بكر فصلى فوجد النبي ﷺ من نفسه خفة فخرج يهادي بين رجلين كأني أنظر إلى رجليه تخطان من الوجع فأراد أبو بكر أن يتأخر فأومأ إليه النبي ﷺ أن مكانك ثم أتي به حتى جلس إلى جنبه
segments.english: We were with ‘A’ishah, may Allah Most High be pleased with her, and we mentioned constancy in prayer and the great regard due to it. She said: When the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, became ill with the illness in which he died, the time for prayer came and the adhan was given. He said: “Tell Abu Bakr to lead the people in prayer.” He was told: “Abu Bakr is a tender-hearted man. If he stands in your place, he will not be able to lead the people in prayer.” He repeated it, and they repeated it to him. He repeated it a third time and said: “You are the women associated with Yusuf. Tell Abu Bakr to lead the people in prayer.” Abu Bakr went out and prayed. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, felt some relief and went out supported between two men. It is as though I can see his feet dragging from the pain. Abu Bakr wanted to move back, but the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, gestured to him to stay in his place. Then he was brought until he sat beside him.

segments.arabic: قيل للأعمش وكان النبي ﷺ يصلي وأبو بكر يصلي بصلاته والناس يصلون بصلاة أبي بكر، فقال برأسه نعم
segments.english: Al-A‘mash was asked: “Was the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, praying, with Abu Bakr praying following his prayer, and the people praying following Abu Bakr’s prayer?” He nodded yes.

segments.arabic: رواه أبو داود عن شعبة عن الأعمش بعضه وزاد أبو معاوية جلس عن يسار أبي بكر فكان أبو بكر يصلي قائما
segments.english: Abu Dawud related part of it from Shu‘bah, from al-A‘mash. Abu Mu‘awiyah added: “He sat to Abu Bakr’s left, and Abu Bakr prayed standing.”

notes: The selected father related to me agrees with the modern print; the historical print uses related to us. Aishah’s full selected honorific is retained. The repeated request and reply, third instruction, support by two men, feet dragging in pain and gesture to stay remain. The question to al-A‘mash and his affirmative nod are separately visible, as are Abu Dawud’s partial route through Shu‘bah and Abu Mu‘awiyah’s additional left-side/standing detail. The English comparisons omit or abbreviate Abu Dawud’s route; it is not dropped.

segments.arabic: [634] حدثنا إبراهيم بن موسى قال: أخبرنا هشام بن يوسف عن معمر عن الزهري قال: أخبرني عبيد الله بن عبد الله قال: قالت عائشة
segments.english: Ibrahim ibn Musa related to us. He said: Hisham ibn Yusuf informed us, from Ma‘mar, from al-Zuhri, who said: ‘Ubayd Allah ibn ‘Abd Allah informed me. He said: ‘A’ishah said:

segments.arabic: لما ثقل النبي ﷺ واشتد وجعه استأذن أزواجه أن يمرض في بيتي فأذن له فخرج بين رجلين تخط رجلاه الأرض وكان بين العباس ورجل آخر
segments.english: When the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, became seriously ill and his pain intensified, he asked his wives’ permission to be cared for in my house, and they gave him permission. He went out between two men, his feet dragging on the ground. He was between al-‘Abbas and another man.

segments.arabic: قال عبيد الله فذكرت ذلك لابن عباس ما قالت عائشة، فقال لي وهل تدري من الرجل الذي لم تسم عائشة قلت لا قال هو علي بن أبي طالب
segments.english: ‘Ubayd Allah said: I mentioned to Ibn ‘Abbas what ‘A’ishah had said. He said to me: “Do you know who the man was whom ‘A’ishah did not name?” I said: “No.” He said: “He was ‘Ali ibn Abi Talib.”

notes: The wives’ permission, Aishah’s house, two supporting men and feet dragging remain. ‘Ali is identified only in the later conversation between ‘Ubayd Allah and Ibn ‘Abbas, presented separately; his name is not inserted into Aishah’s account. The historical print adds an honorific after ‘Ali that is absent from the selected digital and modern texts; it is not imported.

segments.arabic: [635] حدثنا عبد الله بن يوسف قال: أخبرنا مالك عن نافع
segments.english: ‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Nafi‘:

segments.arabic: ان ابن عمر إذن بالصلاة في ليلة ذات برد وريح، ثم قال ألا صلوا في الرحال، ثم قال إن رسول الله ﷺ كان يأمر المؤذن إذا كانت ليلة ذات برد ومطر يقول ألا صلوا في الرحال
segments.english: That Ibn ‘Umar gave the adhan for prayer on a cold, windy night. Then he said: “Listen, pray in your dwellings.” Then he said: “The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to instruct the caller, when it was a cold, rainy night, to say: ‘Listen, pray in your dwellings.’”

notes: The first night is cold and windy; the instruction in the second part concerns a cold and rainy night. Both attention particles and the repeated dwellings instruction remain. The digital إذن is retained in the original Arabic; both inspected prints read أذن with the adhan sense confirmed by context and both English comparisons. This orthographic difference is recorded, not silently rewritten.

segments.arabic: [636] حدثنا إسماعيل قال: حدثني مالك عن ابن شهاب عن محمود بن الربيع الأنصارى
segments.english: Isma‘il related to us. He said: Malik related to me, from Ibn Shihab, from Mahmud ibn al-Rabi‘ al-Ansari:

segments.arabic: أن عتبان بن مالك كان يؤم قومه وهو أعمى وأنه قال لرسول الله ﷺ يا رسول الله إنها تكون الظلمة والسيل وأنا رجل ضرير البصر فصل يا رسول الله في بيتي مكانا أتخذه مصلى فجاءه رسول الله ﷺ، فقال أين تحب أن أصلي فأشار إلى مكان من البيت فصلى فيه رسول الله ﷺ
segments.english: That ‘Itban ibn Malik used to lead his people in prayer, and he was blind. He said to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: “Messenger of Allah, there is darkness and floodwater, and I am a man with impaired sight. Pray, Messenger of Allah, in a place in my house that I can take as a place of prayer.” The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came to him and said: “Where would you like me to pray?” He pointed to a place in the house, and the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prayed there.

notes: The full chain retains Malik related to me. ‘Itban’s leading his people, blindness, darkness and floodwater, request for a particular place in the house, the question about his preference and the eventual prayer there remain. All three selected honorifics remain; the English comparison’s additional introductory eyesight sentence is not inserted.

segments.arabic: [637] حدثنا عبد الله بن عبد الوهاب قال: حدثنا حماد بن زيد قال: حدثنا عبد الحميد صاحب الزيادي قال: سمعت عبد الله بن الحارث قال
segments.english: ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Abd al-Wahhab related to us. He said: Hammad ibn Zayd related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Hamid, the companion of al-Ziyadi, related to us. He said: I heard ‘Abd Allah ibn al-Harith say:

segments.arabic: خطبنا بن عباس في يوم ذي ردغ فأمر المؤذن لما بلغ حي على الصلاة قال قل الصلاة في الرحال فنظر بعضهم إلى بعض فكأنهم أنكروا، فقال: كانكم أنكرتم هذا إن هذا فعله من هو خير مني يعني النبي ﷺ إنها عزمة وإني كرهت أن أحرجكم
segments.english: Ibn ‘Abbas addressed us on a muddy day. When the caller reached “Come to prayer,” he instructed him, saying: “Say: ‘Prayer in the dwellings.’” Some of them looked at one another, as though they disapproved. He said: “It seems that you disapprove of this. Someone better than me did this”—meaning the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. “It is a binding duty, and I disliked putting you in hardship.”

segments.arabic: وعن حماد عن عاصم عن عبد الله بن الحارث عن ابن عباس نحوه غير أنه قال كرهت أن أؤثمكم فتجيئون تدوسون الطين إلى ركبكم
segments.english: And from Hammad, from ‘Asim, from ‘Abd Allah ibn al-Harith, from Ibn ‘Abbas, something similar, except that he said: “I disliked causing you to incur sin, so that you would come trudging through mud up to your knees.”

notes: The first Hammad route retains ‘Abd al-Hamid’s association with al-Ziyadi and the full ‘Abd Allah ibn al-Harith chain. The instruction at Come to prayer, mutual looks, disapproval, better-than-me comparison and source’s Prophet aside remain. The second complete Hammad/‘Asim route and its distinct wording about sin and mud to the knees remain separately visible. The first wording concerns hardship, the second causing sin; they are not harmonized. Binding duty renders the selected عزمة without appending a new ruling.

segments.arabic: [638] حدثنا مسلم بن إبراهيم قال: حدثنا هشام عن يحيى عن أبي سلمة قال:
segments.english: Muslim ibn Ibrahim related to us. He said: Hisham related to us, from Yahya, from Abu Salamah, who said:

segments.arabic: سألت أبا سعيد الخدري، فقال
segments.english: I asked Abu Sa‘id al-Khudri, and he said:

segments.arabic: جاءت سحابة فمطرت حتى سال السقف وكان من جريد النخل فأقيمت الصلاة فرأيت رسول الله ﷺ يسجد في الماء والطين حتى رأيت أثر الطين في جبهته
segments.english: A cloud came and rained until the roof leaked. It was made of palm fronds. The iqamah was given, and I saw the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prostrating in the water and mud, until I saw the mark of mud on his forehead.

notes: Both inspected prints have سال السقف, meaning that the roof leaked; the digital text has سأل السقف. Only this spelling is corrected, through a recorded two-print correction and visible notice with the original preserved. Abu Salamah’s question is retained separately and attributed before Abu Sa‘id’s reply; the comparisons begin directly with the reply. The palm-frond roof, iqamah, water and mud, and mark on the forehead remain.

segments.arabic: [639] حدثنا آدم قال: حدثنا شعبة قال: حدثنا أنس بن سيرين قال: سمعت أنسا يقول:
segments.english: Adam related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us. He said: Anas ibn Sirin related to us. He said: I heard Anas say:

segments.arabic: قال رجل من الأنصار إني لا أستطيع الصلاة معك وكان رجلا ضخما فصنع للنبي ﷺ طعاما فدعاه إلى منزله فبسط له حصيرا ونضح طرف الحصير صلى عليه ركعتين،
segments.english: A man of the Ansar said: “I am unable to pray with you.” He was a large man. He prepared food for the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and invited him to his house. He spread a mat for him and sprinkled water on the edge of the mat. He prayed two rak‘ahs on it.

segments.arabic: فقال رجل من آل الجارود لأنس أكان النبي ﷺ يصلي الضحى قال: ما رأيته صلاها إلا يومئذ
segments.english: A man from the family of al-Jarud said to Anas: “Did the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, pray Duha?” He said: “I never saw him pray it except on that day.”

notes: Anas ibn Sirin’s hearing from Anas remains. The man’s inability to pray with the addressee, his large build, food invitation, spread mat, sprinkled edge and two rak‘ahs remain. The separate question from a man of al-Jarud’s family and Anas’s limited eyewitness answer are not hidden or converted into a general claim.

segments.arabic: [640] حدثنا مسدد قال: حدثنا يحيى عن هشام قال: حدثني أبي قال: سمعت عائشة عن النبي ﷺ أنه قال
segments.english: Musaddad related to us. He said: Yahya related to us, from Hisham, who said: My father related to me. He said: I heard ‘A’ishah relate from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, that he said:

segments.arabic: إذا وضع العشاء وأقيمت الصلاة فابدؤوا بالعشاء
segments.english: “When supper is set out and the iqamah has been given, begin with supper.”

notes: Hisham’s father related to me and I heard ‘Aishah both remain in the full chain. The report contains supper and the iqamah; it does not name a specific obligatory prayer. The unnumbered chapter material is preserved separately and is excluded from the report and its eventual spoken script.

segments.arabic: [641] حدثنا يحيى بن بكير قال: حدثنا الليث عن عقيل عن ابن شهاب عن أنس بن مالك أن رسول الله ﷺ قال:
segments.english: Yahya ibn Bukayr related to us. He said: Al-Layth related to us, from ‘Uqayl, from Ibn Shihab, from Anas ibn Malik, that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

segments.arabic: إذا قدم العشاء فابدؤوا به قبل أن تصلوا صلاة المغرب ولا تعجلوا عن عشائكم
segments.english: “When supper is served, begin with it before you pray the Maghrib prayer, and do not hurry away from your supper.”

notes: The full al-Layth/‘Uqayl/Ibn Shihab/Anas chain remains. This report explicitly names Maghrib, unlike 640. Before praying Maghrib and not hurrying away from supper are both retained.

segments.arabic: [642] حدثنا عبيد بن إسماعيل عن أبي أسامة عن عبيد الله عن نافع عن ابن عمر قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ:
segments.english: ‘Ubayd ibn Isma‘il related to us, from Abu Usamah, from ‘Ubayd Allah, from Nafi‘, from Ibn ‘Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

segments.arabic: إذا وضع عشاء أحدكم وأقيمت الصلاة فابدؤوا بالعشاء ولا يعجل حتى يفرغ منه
segments.english: “When supper is set out for one of you and the iqamah has been given, begin with supper, and he should not hurry until he has finished it.”

segments.arabic: وكان ابن عمر يوضع له الطعام وتقام الصلاة فلا يأتيها حتى يفرغ وإنه ليسمع قراءة الإمام،
segments.english: Food would be set out for Ibn ‘Umar and the iqamah would be given, but he would not go to it until he had finished, while he could hear the imam reciting.

segments.arabic: وقال زهير ووهب بن عثمان عن موسى بن عقبة عن نافع عن ابن عمر قال: قال النبي ﷺ
segments.english: And Zuhayr and Wahb ibn ‘Uthman said: From Musa ibn ‘Uqbah, from Nafi‘, from Ibn ‘Umar, who said: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

segments.arabic: إذا كان أحدكم على الطعام فلا يعجل حتى يقضي حاجته منه وإن أقيمت الصلاة
segments.english: “When one of you is eating, he should not hurry until he has satisfied his need for it, even if the iqamah has been given.”

segments.arabic: رواه إبراهيم بن المنذر عن وهب بن عثمان ووهب مديني
segments.english: Ibrahim ibn al-Mundhir related it from Wahb ibn ‘Uthman, and Wahb is from Madinah.

notes: The first saying, Ibn ‘Umar’s practice, complete Zuhayr/Wahb route and second saying, and Ibrahim ibn al-Mundhir’s final route with Wahb’s Madinan identity remain in source order. Ibn ‘Umar actually hearing the imam is retained; it is not changed to a hypothetical even if. The modern print numbers the additional route 674, while the selected source and historical grouping keep it in this report. Bewley abbreviates the final route to another isnad and the Khan-family comparison omits it; the selected source is complete. The historical print introduces the closing note with Abu ‘Abd Allah said, absent from the selected digital and modern readings.

segments.arabic: [643] حدثنا عبد العزيز بن عبد الله قال: حدثنا إبراهيم عن صالح عن ابن شهاب قال: أخبرني جعفر بن عمرو بن أمية أن أباه قال:
segments.english: ‘Abd al-‘Aziz ibn ‘Abd Allah related to us. He said: Ibrahim related to us, from Salih, from Ibn Shihab, who said: Ja‘far ibn ‘Amr ibn Umayyah informed me that his father said:

segments.arabic: رأيت رسول الله ﷺ يأكل ذراعا يحتز منها فدعي إلى الصلاة فقام فطرح السكين فصلى ولم يتوضأ
segments.english: I saw the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, eating a foreleg, cutting pieces from it. He was called to prayer, so he stood up, put down the knife and prayed without performing ablution.

notes: Ja‘far’s father remains unnamed in the selected chain, which retains informed me. The selected ذراعا is rendered foreleg; neither the comparisons’ shoulder wording nor the Khan-family insertion of sheep is imported. Cutting pieces, being called, standing, setting down the knife and praying without ablution remain.

segments.arabic: [644] حدثنا آدم قال: حدثنا شعبة قال: حدثنا الحكم عن إبراهيم عن الأسود قال:
segments.english: Adam related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us. He said: Al-Hakam related to us, from Ibrahim, from al-Aswad, who said:

segments.arabic: سألت عائشة ما كان النبي ﷺ يصنع في بيته قالت كان يكون في مهنة أهله تعني خدمة أهله فإذا حضرت الصلاة خرج إلى الصلاة
segments.english: I asked ‘A’ishah: “What did the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, do in his house?” She said: “He would be occupied in his family’s work”—meaning serving his family—“and when the time for prayer came, he would go out to prayer.”

notes: Al-Aswad’s question remains visible, followed by Aishah’s reply. The source’s explanatory aside meaning serving his family is retained explicitly within the report, without treating it as a new prophetic saying. The transition when prayer time came remains.

segments.arabic: [645] حدثنا موسى بن إسماعيل قال: حدثنا وهيب قال: حدثنا أيوب عن أبي قلابة قال
segments.english: Musa ibn Isma‘il related to us. He said: Wuhayb related to us. He said: Ayyub related to us, from Abu Qilabah, who said:

segments.arabic: جاءنا مالك بن الحويرث في مسجدنا هذا، فقال إني لأصلي بكم وما أريد الصلاة أصلي كيف رأيت النبي ﷺ يصلي
segments.english: Malik ibn al-Huwayrith came to us in this mosque of ours and said: “I am indeed leading you in prayer, but prayer is not my purpose. I pray as I saw the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, pray.”

segments.arabic: فقلت لأبي قلابة كيف كان يصلي قال مثل شيخنا هذا قال: وكان شيخا يجلس إذا رفع رأسه من السجود قبل أن ينهض في الركعة الأولى
segments.english: I said to Abu Qilabah: “How did he pray?” He said: “Like this elder of ours.” He said: He was an elderly man who would sit when he raised his head from prostration, before standing up in the first rak‘ah.

notes: The selected negative wording about intending prayer is retained. Bewley smooths the wording and the Khan-family comparison supplies a longer teaching explanation. Ibn Hajar discusses the motive and quotes an additional clause in another route; that additional clause is not inserted into this selected report. A separate context note flags this wording for independent review.

The follow-up question to Abu Qilabah and answer about their elder remain visible. The digital and modern print say he was an elderly man; the historical print says the elder. The sitting occurs after raising the head from prostration and before standing in the first rak‘ah. No elder’s name is imported from commentary.

segments.arabic: [646] حدثنا إسحاق بن نصر قال: حدثنا حسين عن زائدة عن عبد الملك بن عمير قال: حدثني أبو بردة عن أبي موسى قال
segments.english: Ishaq ibn Nasr related to us. He said: Husayn related to us, from Za’idah, from ‘Abd al-Malik ibn ‘Umayr, who said: Abu Burdah related to me, from Abu Musa, who said:

segments.arabic: مرض النبي ﷺ فاشتد مرضه، فقال مروا أبا بكر فليصل بالناس قالت عائشة إنه رجل رقيق إذا قام مقامك لم يستطيع أن يصلي بالناس قال مروا أبا بكر فليصل بالناس فعادت، فقال مري أبا بكر فليصل بالناس فإنكن صواحب يوسف فأتاه الرسول فصلى بالناس في حياة النبي ﷺ
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, became ill, and his illness grew severe. He said: “Tell Abu Bakr to lead the people in prayer.” ‘A’ishah said: “He is a tender-hearted man. If he stands in your place, he will not be able to lead the people in prayer.” He said: “Tell Abu Bakr to lead the people in prayer.” She repeated it, and he said: “Tell Abu Bakr to lead the people in prayer. You are the women associated with Yusuf.” The messenger came to him, and he led the people in prayer during the lifetime of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

notes: The selected account begins with the Prophet’s illness and ends with prayer during his lifetime, retaining both honorifics, all three instructions and the repeated objection. The messenger coming to Abu Bakr is retained, although the Bewley comparison omits it. The full chain retains Abu Burdah related to me. The digital grammatical spelling يستطيع differs from the prints يستطع; the selected Arabic remains unchanged.

segments.arabic: [647] حدثنا عبد الله بن يوسف قال: أخبرنا مالك عن هشام بن عروة عن أبيه عن عائشة أم المؤمنين رضى الله تعالى عنها أنها قالت
segments.english: ‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Hisham ibn ‘Urwah, from his father, from ‘A’ishah, Mother of the Believers, may Allah Most High be pleased with her, that she said:

segments.arabic: أن رسول الله ﷺ قال في مرضه مروا أبا بكر يصلي بالناس قالت عائشة قلت: إن أبا بكر إذا قام في مقامك لم يسمع الناس من البكاء فمر عمر فليصل للناس فقالت عائشة فقلت لحفصة قولي له إن أبا بكر إذا قام في مقامك لم يسمع الناس من البكاء فمر عمر فليصل للناس ففعلت حفصة، فقال رسول الله ﷺ: مه إنكن لأنتن صواحب يوسف مروا أبا بكر فليصل للناس فقالت حفصة لعائشة ما كنت لأصيب منك خيرا
segments.english: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said during his illness: “Tell Abu Bakr to lead the people in prayer.” ‘A’ishah said: I said: “If Abu Bakr stands in your place, he will not make the people hear because of his weeping, so tell ‘Umar to lead the people in prayer.” ‘A’ishah said: I said to Hafsah: “Say to him: ‘If Abu Bakr stands in your place, he will not make the people hear because of his weeping, so tell ‘Umar to lead the people in prayer.’” Hafsah did so. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “Stop! You are indeed the women associated with Yusuf. Tell Abu Bakr to lead the people in prayer.” Hafsah said to ‘A’ishah: “I was never to get any good from you.”

notes: Mother of the Believers and Aishah’s complete selected honorific remain. Both full repetitions about Abu Bakr’s weeping and the suggestion to have ‘Umar lead are retained, followed by Hafsah’s action, Stop, the emphatic reply and Hafsah’s final words. The historical print addresses two women in the last command, while the selected digital and modern print use the plural; the wording is not harmonized.

segments.arabic: [648] حدثنا أبو اليمان قال: أخبرنا شعيب عن الزهري قال: أخبرني أنس بن مالك الأنصارى وكان تبع النبي ﷺ وخدمه وصحبه
segments.english: Abu al-Yaman related to us. He said: Shu‘ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: Anas ibn Malik al-Ansari informed me—he had followed the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, served him and kept his company:

segments.arabic: أن أبا بكر كان يصلي لهم في وجع النبي ﷺ الذي توفي فيه حتى إذا كان يوم الإثنين وهم صفوف في الصلاة فكشف النبي ﷺ ستر الحجرة ينظر إلينا وهو قائم كأن وجهه ورقة مصحف ثم تبسم يضحك فهممنا أن نفتتن من الفرح برؤية النبي ﷺ فنكص أبو بكر على عقبيه ليصل الصف وظن أن النبي ﷺ خارج إلى الصلاة فأشار إلينا النبي ﷺ أن أتموا صلاتكم وأرخى الستر فتوفي من يومه
segments.english: That Abu Bakr used to lead them in prayer during the illness of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, in which he died. Then, on Monday, while they were in rows in prayer, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, drew back the curtain of the room and looked towards us while standing. His face was like a page of a copy of the Qur’an. Then he smiled, laughing. We almost became distracted by the joy of seeing the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. Abu Bakr stepped backwards to join the row, thinking that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was coming out to prayer. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, gestured to us to complete our prayer and let the curtain fall. He died that day.

notes: Anas’s following, serving and accompanying the Prophet remain in the complete chain. Monday, the prayer rows, standing at the curtain, the page-of-a-Qur’an comparison, smiling, near distraction through joy, Abu Bakr stepping back, the gesture to finish and death that day remain. All six selected honorifics are preserved; the historical print adds a final honorific absent from the selected digital and modern readings. No historical calendar date or explanatory brightness clause is inserted.

segments.arabic: [649] حدثنا أبو معمر قال: حدثنا عبد الوارث قال: حدثنا عبد العزيز عن أنس قال
segments.english: Abu Ma‘mar related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Warith related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-‘Aziz related to us, from Anas, who said:

segments.arabic: لم يخرج النبي ﷺ ثلاثا فأقيمت الصلاة فذهب أبو بكر يتقدم، فقال نبي الله ﷺ بالحجاب فرفعه فلما وضح وجه النبي ﷺ ما نظرنا منظرا كان أعجب إلينا من وجه النبي ﷺ حين وضح لنا فأومأ النبي ﷺ بيده إلى أبي بكر أن يتقدم وأرخى النبي ﷺ الحجاب فلم يقدر عليه حتى مات
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, did not come out for three days. The iqamah was given, and Abu Bakr went forward. The Prophet of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, took hold of the curtain and lifted it. When the face of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, appeared, we had never seen a sight more pleasing to us than the face of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, when it appeared to us. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, gestured with his hand to Abu Bakr to go forward. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, let the curtain fall, and he could not be reached until he died.

notes: The full Abu Ma‘mar/‘Abd al-Warith/‘Abd al-‘Aziz/Anas chain, three days, movement forward, lifting the curtain, repeated face description, hand gesture and lowering of the curtain remain. All six selected honorifics remain, although Bewley condenses the repeated face description. The selected فلم يقدر عليه is rendered could not be reached, following the passive vocalization in the modern print; the historical print has the first-person نقدر. Both English comparisons render this as not seeing him again. The difference is recorded rather than converting the selected passive wording into a first-person statement.

segments.arabic: [650] حدثنا يحيى بن سليمان قال: حدثنا ابن وهب قال: حدثني يونس عن ابن شهاب عن حمزة بن عبد الله أنه أخبره عن أبيه قال
segments.english: Yahya ibn Sulayman related to us. He said: Ibn Wahb related to us. He said: Yunus related to me, from Ibn Shihab, from Hamzah ibn ‘Abd Allah, that he informed him from his father, who said:

segments.arabic: لما اشتد برسول الله ﷺ وجعه قيل له في الصلاة، فقال مروا أبا بكر فليصل بالناس قالت عائشة إن أبا بكر رجل رقيق إذا قرأ غلبه البكاء، فقال مروه فيصلي فعاودته قال مروه فيصلي إنكن صواحب يوسف
segments.english: When the pain of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, grew severe, prayer was mentioned to him. He said: “Tell Abu Bakr to lead the people in prayer.” ‘A’ishah said: “Abu Bakr is a tender-hearted man. When he recites, weeping overcomes him.” He said: “Tell him, and let him pray.” She repeated it to him. He said: “Tell him, and let him pray. You are the women associated with Yusuf.”

segments.arabic: تابعه الزبيدي وابن أخي الزهري وإسحاق بن يحيى الكلبي عن الزهري، وقال عقيل ومعمر عن الزهري عن حمزة عن النبي ﷺ
segments.english: Al-Zubaydi, the nephew of al-Zuhri, and Ishaq ibn Yahya al-Kalbi corroborated it from al-Zuhri. And ‘Uqayl and Ma‘mar said: From al-Zuhri, from Hamzah, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

notes: The first route retains Ibn Wahb related to us and Yunus related to me; the historical print instead uses Ibn Wahb related to me. Hamzah’s father remains unnamed. The full complaint, all three instructions and repetition remain. The final corroboration names all three transmitters from al-Zuhri; Bewley abbreviates this and Khan omits it. The additional ‘Uqayl/Ma‘mar route goes from Hamzah directly to the Prophet in the selected source, without the father; the missing intermediary is not silently supplied. Both source honorifics remain.

segments.arabic: [651] حدثنا زكريا بن يحيى قال: حدثنا ابن نمير قال: أخبرنا هشام بن عروة عن أبيه عن عائشة قالت
segments.english: Zakariyya ibn Yahya related to us. He said: Ibn Numayr related to us. He said: Hisham ibn ‘Urwah informed us, from his father, from ‘A’ishah, who said:

segments.arabic: أمر رسول الله ﷺ أبا بكر أن يصلي بالناس في مرضه فكان يصلي بهم
segments.english: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, instructed Abu Bakr to lead the people in prayer during his illness, and he used to lead them.

segments.arabic: قال عروة فوجد رسول الله ﷺ في نفسه خفة فخرج فإذا أبو بكر يؤم الناس فلما رآه أبو بكر استأخر فأشار إليه أن كما أنت فجلس رسول الله ﷺ حذاء أبي بكر إلى جنبه فكان أبو بكر يصلي بصلاة رسول الله ﷺ والناس يصلون بصلاة أبي بكر
segments.english: ‘Urwah said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, felt some relief and went out while Abu Bakr was leading the people. When Abu Bakr saw him, he moved back, but he gestured to him to stay as he was. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, sat beside Abu Bakr, at his side. Abu Bakr prayed following the prayer of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and the people prayed following Abu Bakr’s prayer.

notes: The opening attribution to Aishah and the subsequent explicit attribution to ‘Urwah remain distinct, with the latter visible as a transmission note. Four selected honorifics, the gesture to remain, sitting at Abu Bakr’s side and the two layers of following remain. The historical print contains an additional exit clause with an honorific; the selected digital and modern wording is not enlarged. The Khan-family opening narrator label differs from the selected full chain.

segments.arabic: [652] حدثنا عبد الله بن يوسف قال: أخبرنا مالك عن أبي حازم بن دينار عن سهل بن سعد الساعدي
segments.english: ‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Abu Hazim ibn Dinar, from Sahl ibn Sa‘d al-Sa‘idi:

segments.arabic: أن رسول الله ﷺ ذهب إلى بني عمرو بن عوف ليصلح بينهم فحانت الصلاة فجاء المؤذن إلى أبي بكر، فقال أتصلي للناس فأقيم قال: نعم فصلى أبو بكر فجاء رسول الله ﷺ والناس في الصلاة فتخلص حتى وقف في الصف فصفق الناس وكان أبو بكر لا يلتفت في صلاته فلما أكثر الناس التصفيق التفت فرأى رسول الله ﷺ فأشار إليه رسول الله ﷺ أن امكث مكانك فرفع أبو بكر رضى الله تعالى عنه يديه فحمد الله على ما أمره به رسول الله ﷺ من ذلك ثم استأخر أبو بكر حتى استوى في الصف وتقدم رسول الله ﷺ فصلى فلما انصرف قال: يا أبا بكر ما منعك أن تثبت إذ أمرتك، فقال أبو بكر ما كان لابن أبي قحافة أن يصلي بين يدي رسول الله ﷺ، فقال رسول الله ﷺ: ما لي رأيتكم أكثرتم التصفيق من رابه شيء في صلاته فليسبح فإنه إذا سبح التفت إليه وإنما التصفيق للنساء
segments.english: That the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, went to Banu ‘Amr ibn ‘Awf to reconcile them. The time for prayer came, and the caller came to Abu Bakr and said: “Will you lead the people in prayer, so that I may give the iqamah?” He said: “Yes.” Abu Bakr prayed. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came while the people were praying and made his way through until he stood in the row. The people clapped. Abu Bakr did not turn around during his prayer, but when the people clapped repeatedly, he turned and saw the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, gestured to him to stay in his place. Abu Bakr, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, raised his hands and praised Allah for what the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, had instructed him to do. Then Abu Bakr moved back until he stood in the row, and the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, went forward and prayed. When he had finished, he said: “Abu Bakr, what prevented you from remaining when I instructed you?” Abu Bakr said: “It was not for Ibn Abi Quhafah to pray in front of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.” The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “Why did I see you clapping so much? Whoever is troubled by something in his prayer should glorify Allah, for when he glorifies Allah, attention is turned towards him. Clapping is for women.”

notes: The complete reconciliation visit, caller’s question, repeated clapping, initial gesture to remain, Abu Bakr’s raised hands and praise, retreat, eventual lead and final dialogue remain. All eight selected prophetic honorifics and Abu Bakr’s full honorific remain. First row and Abu Bakr’s identity in parentheses are explanatory comparison additions, not selected body words. Glorify Allah renders the Arabic verb without inserting an additional transliterated formula as if separately quoted.

segments.arabic: [653] حدثنا سليمان بن حرب قال: حدثنا حماد بن زيد عن أيوب عن أبي قلابة عن مالك بن الحويرث قال
segments.english: Sulayman ibn Harb related to us. He said: Hammad ibn Zayd related to us, from Ayyub, from Abu Qilabah, from Malik ibn al-Huwayrith, who said:

segments.arabic: قدمنا على النبي ﷺ ونحن شببة فلبثنا عنده نحوا من عشرين ليلة وكان النبي ﷺ رحيما، فقال لو رجعتم إلى بلادكم فعلمتموهم مروهم فليصلوا صلاة كذا في حين كذا وصلاة كذا في حين كذا وإذا حضرت الصلاة فليؤذن لكم أحدكم وليؤمكم أكبركم
segments.english: We came to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, as young men and stayed with him for about twenty nights. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was merciful. He said: “Why not return to your lands and teach them? Instruct them to pray such-and-such a prayer at such-and-such a time, and such-and-such a prayer at such-and-such a time. When the time for prayer comes, let one of you give the adhan for you, and let the oldest of you lead you.”

notes: About twenty nights is retained, rather than Bewley’s twenty days. Both unspecified prayer/time clauses remain, with no actual prayer names or times supplied. The return/teaching suggestion, instruction, adhan and oldest-person clauses remain. The historical print omits the second prayer/time pair, while the digital and modern text contain both; the selected complete wording remains.

segments.arabic: [654] حدثنا معاذ بن أسد أخبرنا عبد الله أخبرنا معمر عن الزهري قال: أخبرني محمود بن الربيع قال: سمعت عتبان بن مالك الأنصارى قال
segments.english: Mu‘adh ibn Asad related to us. ‘Abd Allah informed us. Ma‘mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: Mahmud ibn al-Rabi‘ informed me. He said: I heard ‘Itban ibn Malik al-Ansari say:

segments.arabic: استأذن النبي ﷺ فأذنت له، فقال أين تحب أن أصلي من بيتك فأشرت له إلى المكان الذي أحب فقام وصففنا خلفه ثم سلم وسلمنا
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, asked permission, and I gave him permission. He said: “Where in your house would you like me to pray?” I pointed out the place I liked. He stood, and we formed rows behind him. Then he gave the salutation of peace, and we gave the salutation of peace.

notes: The complete Mu‘adh ibn Asad/‘Abd Allah/Ma‘mar/al-Zuhri/Mahmud/‘Itban chain retains every reporting verb. The historical print names Muhammad ibn al-Rabi‘ while the digital and modern print name Mahmud; the selected name remains. The permission, chosen place, rows and both salutations remain.

segments.arabic: [655] حدثنا أحمد بن يونس قال: حدثنا زائدة عن موسى بن أبي عائشة عن عبيد الله بن عبد الله بن عتبة قال
segments.english: Ahmad ibn Yunus related to us. He said: Za’idah related to us, from Musa ibn Abi ‘A’ishah, from ‘Ubayd Allah ibn ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Utbah, who said:

segments.arabic: دخلت على عائشة فقلت: ألا تحدثيني عن مرض رسول الله ﷺ قالت بلى ثقل النبي ﷺ، فقال أصلى الناس قلنا لا هم ينتظرونك قال ضعوا لي ماء في المخضب قالت ففعلنا فاغتسل فذهب لينوء فأغمي عليه ثم أفاق، فقال ﷺ أصلى الناس قلنا لا هم ينتظرونك يا رسول الله قال ضعوا لي ماء في المخضب قالت فقعد فاغتسل ثم ذهب لينوء فأغمي عليه ثم أفاق، فقال أصلى الناس قلنا لا هم ينتظرونك يا رسول الله، فقال ضعوا لي ماء في المخضب فقعد فاغتسل ثم ذهب لينوء فأغمي عليه ثم أفاق، فقال أصلى الناس فقلنا لا هم ينتظرونك يا رسول الله والناس عكوف في المسجد ينتظرون النبي عليه السلام لصلاة العشاء الآخرة
segments.english: I visited ‘A’ishah and said: “Will you tell me about the illness of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace?” She said: “Yes. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, became seriously ill and said: ‘Have the people prayed?’ We said: ‘No, they are waiting for you.’ He said: ‘Put water for me in the basin.’” She said: “We did so, and he bathed. He tried to rise, but fainted. Then he recovered and said, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: ‘Have the people prayed?’ We said: ‘No, they are waiting for you, Messenger of Allah.’ He said: ‘Put water for me in the basin.’” She said: “He sat and bathed, then tried to rise, but fainted. Then he recovered and said: ‘Have the people prayed?’ We said: ‘No, they are waiting for you, Messenger of Allah.’ He said: ‘Put water for me in the basin.’ He sat and bathed, then tried to rise, but fainted. Then he recovered and said: ‘Have the people prayed?’ We said: ‘No, they are waiting for you, Messenger of Allah.’ The people remained in the mosque, waiting for the Prophet, peace be upon him, for the later ‘Isha’ prayer.”

segments.arabic: فأرسل النبي ﷺ إلى أبي بكر بأن يصلي بالناس فأتاه الرسول، فقال إن رسول الله ﷺ يأمرك أن تصلي بالناس، فقال أبو بكر وكان رجلا رقيقا يا عمر صل بالناس، فقال له عمر أنت أحق بذلك فصلى أبو بكر تلك الأيام ثم إن النبي ﷺ وجد من نفسه خفة فخرج بين رجلين أحدهما العباس لصلاة الظهر وأبو بكر يصلي بالناس فلما رآه أبو بكر ذهب ليتأخر فأومأ إليه النبي ﷺ بأن لا يتأخر قال أجلساني إلى جنبه فأجلساه إلى جنب أبي بكر قال: فجعل أبو بكر يصلي وهو يأتم بصلاة النبي ﷺ والناس بصلاة أبي بكر والنبي ﷺ قاعد
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, sent to Abu Bakr to lead the people in prayer. The messenger came to him and said: “The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, instructs you to lead the people in prayer.” Abu Bakr, who was a tender-hearted man, said: “‘Umar, lead the people in prayer.” ‘Umar said to him: “You have more right to do so.” Abu Bakr led the prayers during those days. Then the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, felt some relief and went out between two men, one of them al-‘Abbas, for the Zuhr prayer. Abu Bakr was leading the people. When Abu Bakr saw him, he began to move back, but the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, gestured to him not to move back. He said: “Seat me beside him.” They seated him beside Abu Bakr. He said: Abu Bakr then prayed following the prayer of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and the people followed Abu Bakr’s prayer, while the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was seated.

segments.arabic: قال عبيد الله فدخلت على عبد الله بن عباس فقلت له ألا أعرض عليك ما حدثتني عائشة عن مرض النبي ﷺ قال: هات فعرضت عليه حديثها فما أنكر شيئا غير أنه قال أسمت لك الرجل الذي كان مع العباس قلت لا قال هو علي
segments.english: ‘Ubayd Allah said: I visited ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Abbas and said to him: “Shall I present to you what ‘A’ishah related to me about the illness of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace?” He said: “Go ahead.” I presented her account to him, and he disputed nothing, except that he said: “Did she name for you the man who was with al-‘Abbas?” I said: “No.” He said: “He was ‘Ali.”

notes: All four questions about whether the people have prayed, all three water requests, bathing, attempts to rise and fainting remain. The first answer does not add Messenger of Allah from an English comparison. Ten selected ﷺ honorifics and the distinct عليه السلام remain. The transition from the later ‘Isha’ prayer to Zuhr, Abu Bakr’s invitation to ‘Umar, reply, supported exit and seated following remain complete.

The final ‘Ubayd Allah/Ibn ‘Abbas conversation is separately visible, with the exact name ‘Ali rather than adding his patronymic. The historical print expands that name and has additional or different honorific wording; the selected digital and modern reading remains. No repeated sequence is compressed into again or three times in place of its actual words.

segments.arabic: [656] حدثنا عبد الله بن يوسف قال: أخبرنا مالك عن هشام بن عروة عن أبيه عن عائشة أم المؤمنين أنها قالت
segments.english: ‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Hisham ibn ‘Urwah, from his father, from ‘A’ishah, Mother of the Believers, that she said:

segments.arabic: صلى رسول الله ﷺ في بيته وهو شاك فصلى جالسا وصلى وراءه قوم قياما فأشار إليهم أن اجلسوا فلما انصرف قال إنما جعل الإمام ليؤتم به فإذا ركع فاركعوا وإذا رفع فارفعوا وإذا صلى جالسا فصلوا جلوسا
segments.english: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prayed in his house while ill. He prayed sitting, and people behind him prayed standing. He gestured to them to sit. When he had finished, he said: “The imam is appointed only to be followed. When he bows, bow; when he rises, rise; and when he prays sitting, pray sitting.”

notes: The Mother of the Believers title, illness, sitting, people standing behind, sitting gesture and three follow-the-imam clauses remain. The historical print and Khan-family comparison include a hearing/praise response clause not present in the selected digital or modern text; it is not imported. It appears explicitly in the following selected report 657.

segments.arabic: [657] حدثنا عبد الله بن يوسف قال: أخبرنا مالك عن ابن شهاب عن أنس بن مالك
segments.english: ‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Ibn Shihab, from Anas ibn Malik:

segments.arabic: أن رسول الله ﷺ ركب فرسا فصرع عنه فجحش شقه الأيمن فصلى صلاة من الصلوات وهو قاعد فصلينا وراءه قعودا فلما انصرف قال إنما جعل الإمام ليؤتم به فإذا صلى قائما فصلوا قياما فإذا ركع فاركعوا وإذا رفع فارفعوا وإذا قال سمع الله لمن حمده فقولوا ربنا ولك الحمد وإذا صلى قائما فصلوا قياما وإذا صلى جالسا فصلوا جلوسا أجمعون
segments.english: That the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, rode a horse and was thrown from it, grazing his right side. He performed one of the prayers sitting, and we prayed behind him sitting. When he had finished, he said: “The imam is appointed only to be followed. When he prays standing, pray standing. When he bows, bow; when he rises, rise; and when he says, ‘Allah hears whoever praises Him,’ say, ‘Our Lord, and to You belongs praise.’ When he prays standing, pray standing; and when he prays sitting, all of you pray sitting.”

segments.arabic: قال أبو عبد الله قال الحميدي قوله إذا صلى جالسا فصلوا جلوسا هو في مرضه القديم ثم صلى بعد ذلك النبي ﷺ جالسا والناس خلفه قياما لم يأمرهم بالقعود وإنما يؤخذ بالآخر فالآخر من فعل النبي ﷺ
segments.english: Abu ‘Abd Allah said: Al-Humaydi said: His words, “When he prays sitting, pray sitting,” concern his earlier illness. After that, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prayed sitting while the people behind him were standing, and he did not instruct them to sit. What is taken is the latest, then the latest, of the actions of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

notes: The horse, fall, right-side graze, seated prayer and the complete statement remain. The standing instruction occurs twice in the selected digital and modern text; both occurrences remain, although the historical print has it once. The full Abu ‘Abd Allah/al-Humaydi attribution and closing chronology comment remain separately visible. The Khan-family comparison labels the commentator Humaid; the selected Arabic names al-Humaydi.

The historical print has additional abrogation wording and an additional closing explanation absent from the selected digital and modern reading. Those are recorded as variants, not imported as report text. The selected latest-then-latest repetition remains, without turning the narrator’s comment into an app-issued ruling.

segments.arabic: [658] حدثنا مسدد قال: حدثنا يحيى بن سعيد عن سفيان قال: حدثني أبو إسحاق قال: حدثني عبد الله بن يزيد قال: حدثني البراء وهو غير كذوب قال:
segments.english: Musaddad related to us. He said: Yahya ibn Sa‘id related to us, from Sufyan, who said: Abu Ishaq related to me. He said: ‘Abd Allah ibn Yazid related to me. He said: Al-Bara’ related to me—and he was not a liar—who said:

segments.arabic: كان رسول الله ﷺ إذا قال سمع الله لمن حمده لم يحن أحد منا ظهره حتى يقع النبي ﷺ ساجدا ثم نقع سجودا بعده
segments.english: When the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, “Allah hears whoever praises Him,” none of us bent his back until the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, had gone down in prostration. Then we went down in prostration after him.

segments.arabic: حدثنا أبو نعيم عن سفيان عن أبي إسحاق نحوه بهذا
segments.english: Abu Nu‘aym related to us, from Sufyan, from Abu Ishaq, something similar to this.

segments.arabic: [659] حدثنا حجاج بن منهال قال: حدثنا شعبة عن محمد بن زياد سمعت أبا هريرة عن النبي ﷺ، وقال:
segments.english: Hajjaj ibn Minhal related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad: I heard Abu Hurayrah relate from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

segments.arabic: أما يخشى أحدكم أو ألا يخشى أحدكم إذا رفع رأسه قبل الإمام أن يجعل الله رأسه رأس حمار أو يجعل الله صورته صورة حمار
segments.english: “Does one of you not fear—or: Does one of you not fear—when he raises his head before the imam, that Allah may turn his head into a donkey’s head, or turn his form into the form of a donkey?”

notes: Both source alternatives أما يخشى and ألا يخشى are retained as repeated equivalent English questions with or. The head/form alternatives also remain. The Khan-family body is individually matched to 1.11.660, not 1.11.659, which is an unnumbered pointer belonging to the previous comparison sequence. No face-only narrowing replaces the selected form wording.

segments.arabic: [660] حدثنا إبراهيم بن المنذر قال: حدثنا أنس بن عياض عن عبيد الله عن نافع عن ابن عمر قال
segments.english: Ibrahim ibn al-Mundhir related to us. He said: Anas ibn ‘Iyad related to us, from ‘Ubayd Allah, from Nafi‘, from Ibn ‘Umar, who said:

segments.arabic: لما قدم المهاجرون الأولون العصبة موضع بقباء قبل مقدم رسول الله ﷺ كان يؤمهم سالم مولى أبي حذيفة وكان أكثرهم قرآنا
segments.english: When the earliest emigrants came to al-‘Usbah, a place at Quba’, before the arrival of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, Salim, the freedman of Abu Hudhayfah, used to lead them in prayer. He knew the most Qur’an among them.

notes: The earliest emigrants, al-‘Usbah as a place at Quba’, arrival before the Messenger and Salim’s relationship to Abu Hudhayfah remain. The selected Arabic says mawla; freedman is the working rendering, as in Bewley, while Khan says slave. The historical print expands Ibn ‘Umar’s name; no extra name is inserted. Khan is individually matched at 1.11.661.

segments.arabic: [661] حدثنا محمد بن بشار حدثنا يحيى حدثنا شعبة قال: حدثني أبو التياح عن أنس عن النبي ﷺ قال:
segments.english: Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us. Yahya related to us. Shu‘bah related to us. He said: Abu al-Tayyah related to me, from Anas, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

segments.arabic: اسمعوا وأطيعوا وإن استعمل حبشي كأن رأسه زبيبة
segments.english: “Listen and obey, even if an Abyssinian whose head is like a raisin is appointed.”

notes: The full chain retains Muhammad ibn Bashshar, Yahya, Shu‘bah, Abu al-Tayyah and Anas. The selected Arabic does not add slave or a modern racial classification. Abyssinian and the raisin comparison remain unchanged in sense; the app adds no new characterization. Khan is individually matched at 1.11.662.

segments.arabic: [662] حدثنا الفضل بن سهل قال: حدثنا الحسن بن موسى الأشيب قال: حدثنا عبد الرحمن بن عبد الله بن دينار عن زيد بن أسلم عن عطاء بن يسار عن أبي هريرة أن رسول الله ﷺ قال:
segments.english: Al-Fadl ibn Sahl related to us. He said: Al-Hasan ibn Musa al-Ashyab related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn ‘Abd Allah ibn Dinar related to us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from ‘Ata’ ibn Yasar, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

segments.arabic: يصلون لكم فإن أصابوا فلكم وإن أخطؤوا فلكم وعليهم
segments.english: “They lead prayer for you. If they get it right, it is for you; if they get it wrong, it is for you and against them.”

notes: The full chain retains al-Ashyab and ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn ‘Abd Allah ibn Dinar. Both if-clauses and the source’s for-you/against-them contrast remain. The comparison texts explicitly supply reward, sin and reward for the imam; those explanatory nouns and the extra beneficiary are not inserted into the selected elliptical wording. segments.arabic: [663] قال أبو عبد الله، وقال لنا محمد بن يوسف حدثنا الأوزاعي حدثنا الزهري عن حميد بن عبد الرحمن عن عبيد الله بن عدي بن خيار
segments.english: Abu ‘Abd Allah said: And Muhammad ibn Yusuf said to us: Al-Awza‘i related to us. Al-Zuhri related to us, from Humayd ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman, from ‘Ubayd Allah ibn ‘Adi ibn Khiyar:

segments.arabic: أنه دخل على عثمان بن عفان رضى الله تعالى عنه وهو محصور، فقال إنك إمام عامة ونزل بك ما ترى ويصلي لنا إمام فتنة ونتحرج، فقال الصلاة أحسن ما يعمل الناس فإذا أحسن الناس فأحسن معهم وإذا أساؤوا فاجتنب إساءتهم،
segments.english: That he visited ‘Uthman ibn ‘Affan, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, while he was under siege. He said: “You are the imam of the community, and what you see has befallen you. An imam involved in turmoil leads us in prayer, and we feel uneasy about it.” He said: “Prayer is the best of what people do. When people do good, do good with them; when they do wrong, avoid their wrongdoing.”

segments.arabic: وقال الزبيدي قال الزهري لا نرى أن يصلي خلف المخنث إلا من ضرورة لابد منها
segments.english: And al-Zubaydi said: Al-Zuhri said: “We do not consider that prayer should be performed behind an effeminate man except out of an unavoidable necessity.”

comparisons.note: The checked consecutive records move from the imam’s correct/mistaken prayer to the Prophet addressing Abu Dharr. This Uthman account and al-Zuhri’s closing comment are not present in that sequence. No matching reference is assigned.

notes: The complete compiler attribution, Muhammad ibn Yusuf said to us, both related-to-us links and ‘Ubayd Allah ibn ‘Adi ibn Khiyar name remain. The report concerns ‘Uthman under siege; it is not attributed to the Prophet. His complete selected honorific and what you see remain. The closing al-Zubaydi/al-Zuhri comment remains separately visible.

Both inspected Arabic prints read المخنث, while the digital paragraph has المحنث. Only that spelling is corrected with declared two-print evidence and a visible notice; the unchanged original remains accessible. Effeminate man follows one recorded lexical sense and Bewley’s comparison. Ibn Hajar records differing readings/senses; the working choice does not substitute a modern identity label. Independent lexical review remains pending.

segments.arabic: [664] حدثنا محمد بن أبان حدثنا غندر عن شعبة عن أبي التياح أنه سمع أنس بن مالك قال النبي ﷺ لأبي ذر
segments.english: Muhammad ibn Aban related to us. Ghundar related to us, from Shu‘bah, from Abu al-Tayyah, that he heard Anas ibn Malik say: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said to Abu Dharr:

segments.arabic: اسمع وأطع ولو لحبشي كأن رأسه زبيبة
segments.english: “Listen and obey, even an Abyssinian whose head is like a raisin.”

comparisons.note: This comparison points back to 661 and gives only an abbreviated attribution; its wording must not replace the selected complete Prophet-to-Abu-Dharr report.

notes: The complete Abu al-Tayyah/Anas route and the Prophet addressing Abu Dharr remain.
